title.narrative: Integrated WASH and Education emergency response to the floods in the Far North of Cameroon

description.narrative: The Far North region of Cameroon is facing a complex humanitarian crisis marked by conflict, instability, climatic shocks, and disease outbreaks, leaving 1.2 million people in need of humanitarian assistance. Since July 2024, heavy rains have led to flooding in several localities in the Far North. As of 3 October 2024, data from local authorities and OCHA indicate that 67,545 households, comprising 356,730 people, have been affected. The floods have resulted in the loss of 5,278 heads of livestock and the destruction of 82,509 hectares of agricultural land. Furthermore, an estimated 262 schools were destroyed or cut off by the floods, affecting over 103,906 students and 1,418 teachers in the Mayo-Danay and Logone-et-Chari divisions alone. In September 2024, over 40 per cent of boreholes, the primary source of drinking water, were either inaccessible, submerged, or damaged. Latrines are flooded and/or inaccessible to households. The CERF RR project aims to address the urgent WASH and education needs of those affected by floods, including people affected who remained in the flooded areas internally displaced persons (IDPs), and host populations, especially children, in the flood-affected areas of Cameroon’s Far North region. Thus, 70,000 vulnerable IDPs and host populations (19,000 girls, 18,000 boys, 16,000 women and 17,000 men) in the targeted areas, will receive emergency lifesaving WASH interventions. The same communities are also targeted for Education services. The WASH component of the project will focus on emergency repair of water points, latrine construction and hygiene promotion including awareness building on sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and GBV prevention. The Education component of this project will focus on delivering an emergency response to support the continuity of educational activities for the children whose schools were affected by floods. The project will provide 10 temporary learning spaces as well as teaching, recreational and learning materials for 13,500 students and 150 teachers from targeted communities. This will also ensure access to education for children who have dropped out school due to the floods, reduce the pressure on the affected structures and improve teaching and learning conditions. To leverage on the complementarity with the WASH component, the targeted schools will also benefit from the provision of WASH services through the delivery of a more holistic package. Flood-resilient gender-sensitive latrines will be built in assisted schools. Young builders from the municipality affected will be trained in the construction of latrines using local materials. For families who host IDPs, support in sanitation kits (shovels, picks, slabs, etc.) will be provided for the construction/rehabilitation of their latrines. The distribution of hygiene kits coupled with hygiene promotion including GBV and SEA awareness raising will be provided to IDPs and host community households. Moreover, as part of the WASH component, menstrual hygiene management kits will be distributed to girl children and adolescents enrolled in the assisted schools. 200 teachers and members from Community Participative Structures are expected to receive capacity building on psychosocial support and life-saving contents to enhance the resilience of targeted educational communities. Using alternative funding sources, UNICEF will target the same communities also with nutrition, health, and child protection interventions to provide a multisectoral package to those affected.
